title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Priya Desai
summary: A single reference for Redwood Inference company-wide policies and standard operating procedures covering access & permissions, change management, data handling, procurement & expenses, vendor lifecycle, travel guidance, and the canonical internal templates.
body:
Purpose

This document consolidates company-wide policies and standard operating procedures (SOPs) used across Redwood Inference. The goal is to provide clear, auditable rules and step-by-step procedures that balance security, speed of operations, and compliance.

Scope

Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and vendors with corporate accounts, and covers the following areas: access & permissions, change management, data management and retention, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and internal templates. Exceptions must be approved by the owner team and recorded in the related_pages section.

Ownership and roles

- Policy owner: People Ops (primary); Security & Compliance and Finance & Legal are cross-functional owners for specific sections.
- Approvers: Team manager -> People Ops (for role changes) or Finance & Legal (for contractual/procurement changes) -> Executive sponsor for exceptions above thresholds.
- Operational owners: Service owners and platform teams are responsible for executing technical change and access reviews.

1) Access & permissions

Principles:
- Least privilege by default.
- Role-based access controls (RBAC) where possible; temporary elevated access via just-in-time (JIT) workflows.
- Separation of duties for sensitive systems (finance, payroll, secrets).

Access levels (examples):
- Viewer: read-only to service dashboards and documentation.
- Contributor: deploy and modify non-sensitive configs.
- Admin: full control; requires manager approval + People Ops review.
- Privileged: access to secrets/KMS/HSM or production write paths; requires two-step approval and 90-day audit logging.

Standard request flow:
1. Requester submits an access request via internal ticketing system (link: /internal/tools/access-requests).
2. Requester’s manager approves (1st line).
3. Resource owner approves (2nd line).
4. People Ops or Security performs policy checks for privileged access.
5. Access is provisioned and logged.

Temporary access and JIT:
- Temporary access durations: default 24 hours for admins, up to 7 days for elevated engineering tasks with justification.
- All temporary grants must include purpose and expected rollback time.

Periodic review:
- Quarterly access reviews for high-risk groups (finance, security, production admins).
- Semi-annual company-wide role audits.
- Automated alerts for orphaned accounts (inactive > 60 days).

2) Change management

Change categories:
- Standard change: documented, low-risk, pre-authorized operational tasks (e.g., routine config updates).
- Normal change: requires change ticket, impact assessment, and approval by change owner.
- Emergency change: immediate remediation required to protect service or security; documented post-facto and reviewed by Change Advisory Board (CAB).

Process for normal changes:
1. Create a change ticket in the change management system with the following fields: owner, rollback plan, test plan, risk rating (low/medium/high), scheduled window.
2. Service owner and engineering manager review.
3. CAB reviews medium/high-risk changes at least 48 hours before scheduled window.
4. Execute change during approved window; monitor health metrics for at least one SLA cycle post-change.
5. Close ticket with post-change verification and update runbooks if needed.

Emergency change flow:
- Notify CAB on-call, execute mitigation, then perform post-incident change record within 24 hours. A full post-implementation review is required within 5 business days.

Rollback and verification:
- Every change must include a clear rollback plan with estimated time-to-restore and verification checklist.
- If rollback occurs, an incident review must be created and attached to the change ticket.

3) Data management and classification

Data classification levels (company-wide):
- Public: intended for public consumption.
- Internal: company-internal data with low sensitivity.
- Confidential: business-sensitive data (product roadmaps, unreleased pricing).
- Restricted: PII, customer-provided sensitive data, regulated data (PCI, HIPAA) — requires strict controls.

Data handling rules:
- Restricted data must be stored in approved systems with encryption at rest and in transit (TLS 1.2+).
- No restricted data in personal email or unmanaged devices.
- Use customer-specific VPC/private deployments for regulated workloads; document the handling plan in the customer contract.

Retention and deletion:
- Default retention: Internal data 2 years, Confidential 5 years, Restricted as required by contract/regulation.
- Automated retention policies should be applied (S3 Lifecycle, DB TTLs).
- Data deletion requests (customer or employee data) must follow the data subject request procedure: submit form -> Legal review -> Delete/Anonymize -> Audit log entry.

Backups and DR:
- Critical production data: daily backups, 90-day on-line retention, 1-year offsite retention for long-term compliance where required.
- Quarterly restore tests for critical services; documented in eng-infra/runbooks.

Logging and audit:
- Audit logs for privileged actions must be retained for 1 year and accessible to Security & Compliance.
- Access logs for production systems must be immutable (WORM) where regulation mandates.

4) Procurement & expenses

Procurement thresholds and approvals (typical):
- <$5,000: Manager approval.
- $5,000–$50,000: Manager + People Ops/Finance review.
- >$50,000: Manager + Finance + Legal sign-off and Executive sponsor.

Procurement process (SaaS or hardware):
1. Raise purchase request with vendor, itemized quote, business justification, and budget code.
2. Finance verifies budget and issues PO when required.
3. Contracts > $50k routed to Legal for review and signature.
4. Receiving and asset tagging for hardware purchases; record vendor in vendor management system.

Expense reimbursement:
- Submit expenses within 30 days using the travel & expense system with receipts.
- Approvers: direct manager for normal travel and People Ops for relocation or one-time allowances.
- Non-reimbursable items: personal entertainment, alcohol (unless approved for client events), fines/tickets.

Corporate card policy:
- Cards are issued on an as-needed basis; cardholders must complete a brief training and reconcile monthly transactions.

5) Vendor management

Onboarding checklist:
- Vendor profile created in vendor system with contact, tax forms, and security questionnaire.
- Security review: for vendors accessing sensitive data, Security must complete a risk assessment and may require SOC2/ISO evidence.
- Contract: include data processing addendum (DPA), breach notification timelines, and termination clauses.

Ongoing management:
- Quarterly vendor health checks for strategic vendors; annual security re-evaluation for vendors with access to restricted data.
- Renewal timeline: renewals initiated 90 days prior to contract expiry with commercial and security reviews.

Offboarding:
- Revoke all access, return or destroy customer data per contract, and create an offboarding checklist in the vendor record.

6) Travel policy

Booking and approvals:
- Travel must be booked at least 7 days in advance where possible.
- Manager approval required for all travel; People Ops approval for international travel that requires visas.

Allowances and reimbursements:
- Per diem guidelines: meals up to $60/day domestic, $100/day international (exceptions for high-cost cities require manager pre-approval).
- Hotel: select preferred vendors when available; upgrades reimbursed only with prior approval.

Safety and incident reporting:
- Employees traveling on company business must enroll in the travel safety program.
- Report incidents to People Ops and Security within 24 hours.

7) Internal templates and forms

Canonical templates (links):
- Access request template: /confluence/templates/access-request-template
- Change request template: /confluence/templates/change-request-template
- Vendor onboarding checklist: /confluence/templates/vendor-onboarding-checklist
- Procurement request form: /confluence/templates/purchase-request-form
- Expense form and travel checklist: /confluence/templates/expense-form

Usage guidance:
- All templates must be used for documented approvals; ad-hoc approvals require a documented exception and an accompanying email chain saved to the ticket.

8) Procedures and escalation

Escalation matrix (examples):
- Access denied or data exposure: contact Security on-call immediately; if customer-impacting, follow oncall-and-incident-response incident_process.
- Procurement delays affecting delivery: escalate to Finance and commercial lead; for >10 business day delays, inform People Ops.

SOP for policy exception requests:
1. Submit exception request with justification and compensating controls.
2. Manager and owner-team review.
3. If approved, record exception in related_pages and schedule a re-review date (max 6 months).

9) Metrics, audit, and compliance

Key metrics to track:
- Number of privileged accounts and average time to deprovision.
- % of changes with complete rollback plans.
- Age of open procurement requests beyond SLA.
- Vendor compliance score (based on security questionnaire).

Audit cadence:
- Internal audits: semi-annual for access and procurement.
- External audits: as required by customer contracts (SOC2/ISO).

Appendix: quick references and SLA windows

- Access provisioning SLA: standard requests 3 business days; privileged requests 7 business days.
- Change approval SLA: standard changes approved within 48 hours; CAB review scheduled 48+ hours before window.
- Procurement SLAs: routine purchases processed in 10 business days; contracts (> $50k) processed in 30–45 business days depending on negotiation.

Contact and escalation points

- People Ops (policy owner): people-ops@redwood.ai
- Security & Compliance: security@redwood.ai
- Finance & Legal: finance-legal@redwood.ai

Related pages and artifacts

- System runbooks: /confluence/eng-infra/runbooks
- RBAC and auth architecture: /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth
- Vendor contract templates: /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process

Change log

End of document
